name: Rome
note: The historic centre of Rome from OpenStreetMap, on the shared engine, with its real hills: inside the Aurelian Walls from the Vatican and Castel Sant'Angelo across the Tiber to the Lateran, and from Piazza del Popolo down past the Forum and the Colosseum to the Baths of Caracalla. The buildings that are shapes rather than heights - the Colosseum, the Pantheon, St Peter's, the domes - are modelled in src/rome/landmarks.js from their published dimensions. Data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
defaultView: Over the Forum to the Colosseum
attribution: Rome: map data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL. Elevation: AWS Terrain Tiles (SRTM). Built by tools/build-osm-city.py.

fetch._: the whole centre is a detail zone: every building is kept

terrain._: the seven hills, the Janiculum and the Pincian: elevation from tools/fetch-terrain.py

filter._: the elevation carries the city's roofs and domes, up to 16 m: tools/filter-terrain.py, tools/build-osm-city.py

defaultHeights._: Rome's untagged buildings are palazzi of four to six floors, not houses: see tools/build-osm-city.py

facade._: palazzo proportions: tall storeys, windows wide apart, stone frames and shutters

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

landmarks.name: The Colosseum
landmarks.info: The Flavian Amphitheatre, finished in AD 80: an ellipse 189 by 156 m and 48 m high, eighty arches round, for fifty thousand people. Half its outer ring came down in the earthquake of 1349 and became the city's palaces.

landmarks.name: The Pantheon
landmarks.info: Hadrian's temple to all the gods, about AD 125: a dome of unreinforced concrete 43.3 m across, open to the sky at the oculus, as high as it is wide. The inscription names Agrippa, who built the temple it replaced.

landmarks.name: St Peter's Basilica
landmarks.info: The basilica over the tomb of St Peter, 1506 to 1626: Bramante, Raphael, Sangallo, Michelangelo (the dome), Maderno (the nave and the front), Bernini. 136.6 m to the cross on the lantern, the tallest dome in the world.

landmarks.name: St Peter's Square
landmarks.info: Bernini's oval, 1656 to 1667: two arms of colonnade four columns deep - 284 columns, 140 saints on the balustrade - reaching out, he said, like the arms of the Church. The obelisk in the middle came from Egypt under Caligula.

landmarks.name: Altare della Patria
landmarks.info: The monument to Victor Emmanuel II, first king of Italy, 1885 to 1935: white Botticino marble, 135 m wide and 81 m high to its quadrigas. Romans call it the wedding cake, or the typewriter.

landmarks.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
landmarks.info: Hadrian's mausoleum, AD 139; then a fortress, a papal refuge and a prison. The bronze archangel on top commemorates the vision of 590 that ended a plague.

landmarks.name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
landmarks.info: Hadrian's bridge to his tomb, AD 134, with Bernini's ten angels carrying the instruments of the Passion, 1669.

landmarks.name: The Trevi Fountain
landmarks.info: Salvi's fountain, 1732 to 1762, at the end of the Aqua Virgo, an aqueduct of 19 BC that still runs. A coin over the shoulder, and you will come back to Rome.

landmarks.name: Sant'Agnese in Agone
landmarks.info: Borromini's church on Piazza Navona, 1652 to 1672, its front curving in between two bell towers, across from Bernini's fountain.

landmarks.name: Fountain of the Four Rivers
landmarks.info: Bernini, 1651: the Nile, the Ganges, the Danube and the Plata on a hollow rock, carrying an Egyptian-style obelisk made in Rome for Domitian.

landmarks.name: Campo de' Fiori
landmarks.info: The market every morning but Sunday; in the middle, the hooded Giordano Bruno (Ettore Ferrari, 1889), where he was burned in 1600.

landmarks.name: Ponte degli Annibaldi
landmarks.info: Francesco Cellini with Insula: a footbridge over Via degli Annibaldi that puts back the line of Via della Polveriera, cut by the street in the last century. The view of the Colosseum from it is the postcard one.

landmarks.name: Fontana del Pantheon
landmarks.info: Giacomo della Porta, 1575; Clement XI set the obelisk of Rameses II (the Macuteo) on it in 1711.

landmarks.name: Fontana della Barcaccia
landmarks.info: Pietro and Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 1629: a half-sunk boat at the foot of the Spanish Steps, low because the Acqua Vergine has little head.

landmarks.name: Temple of Saturn
landmarks.info: Eight columns of the temple of Saturn, rebuilt after a fire in the fourth century; the state treasury was kept in its podium.

landmarks.name: Temple of Castor and Pollux
landmarks.info: Three Corinthian columns on a podium seven metres high: what is left of the temple of the Dioscuri, rebuilt by Tiberius in AD 6.

landmarks.name: Temple of Vespasian
landmarks.info: Three columns at the foot of the Capitoline, the corner of a temple to the deified Vespasian.

landmarks.name: Temple of Antoninus and Faustina
landmarks.info: Built by Antoninus Pius for his wife in AD 141, a church since the seventh century: San Lorenzo in Miranda's baroque front stands behind the ancient portico.

landmarks.name: Arch of Septimius Severus
landmarks.info: AD 203, for the emperor's victories over the Parthians: three arches, the columns standing free on their pedestals.

landmarks.name: Arch of Titus
landmarks.info: About AD 81, for the sack of Jerusalem; inside the arch the spoils of the Temple, the menorah carried in triumph.

landmarks.name: Arch of Constantine
landmarks.info: AD 315, for Constantine's victory at the Milvian Bridge, built half from the reliefs of older monuments; the Dacian prisoners on the attic came from Trajan's.

landmarks.name: Basilica of Maxentius
landmarks.info: Begun by Maxentius and finished by Constantine: three of its great coffered vaults still stand, twenty metres across.

landmarks.name: Trajan's Column
landmarks.info: AD 113: a spiral frieze two hundred metres long winds twenty-three times up the shaft, the story of the Dacian wars in 2,600 figures. St Peter on top since 1587.

landmarks.name: Column of Marcus Aurelius
landmarks.info: Piazza Colonna, after AD 180: the Marcomannic wars wound up its shaft; St Paul on top since 1589.

landmarks.name: Theatre of Marcellus
landmarks.info: Finished by Augustus in 13 BC and named for his nephew: the arcades are the model the Colosseum followed. The Orsini built a palazzo into the top in the sixteenth century.

landmarks.name: Pyramid of Cestius
landmarks.info: The tomb of the magistrate Gaius Cestius, about 12 BC, built in 330 days in the Egyptian fashion and later set into the Aurelian Walls.

landmarks.name: The Spanish Steps
landmarks.info: 135 steps from Piazza di Spagna to Trinità dei Monti, 1723 to 1725, paid for by a French diplomat; the Barcaccia at their foot, the obelisk at their top.

landmarks.name: Obelisk of Piazza del Popolo
landmarks.info: Ramesses II's obelisk from Heliopolis, brought to Rome by Augustus for the Circus Maximus, set up here in 1589.

landmarks.name: Lateran Obelisk
landmarks.info: The tallest obelisk in the world: Thutmose III's, from Karnak, 32 m of red granite, brought to Rome in 357 for the Circus Maximus.

landmarks.name: Obelisk of Montecitorio
landmarks.info: Psammetichus II's obelisk, which Augustus used as the pointer of a great sundial on the Campus Martius.

landmarks.name: Esquiline Obelisk
landmarks.info: One of a pair that stood at the mausoleum of Augustus; the other is on the Quirinal.

landmarks.name: Quirinal Obelisk
landmarks.info: The other of Augustus's pair, between the Dioscuri and their horses.

landmarks.name: Sant'Andrea della Valle
landmarks.info: The second highest dome in Rome after St Peter's (1622), and the setting of the first act of Tosca.

landmarks.name: Il Gesù
landmarks.info: The mother church of the Jesuits, 1568 to 1580, the model for baroque churches everywhere.

landmarks.name: Santi Ambrogio e Carlo al Corso
landmarks.info: Pietro da Cortona's dome, 1668, on the Corso: the third largest in Rome.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria di Loreto
landmarks.info: One of the twin domes beside Trajan's Column, by Antonio da Sangallo the Younger.

landmarks.name: Santissimo Nome di Maria al Foro Traiano
landmarks.info: The other twin dome at Trajan's Forum, 1736.

landmarks.name: San Carlo ai Catinari
landmarks.info: The Barnabites' church, 1612 to 1620, named for the basin makers of the street.

landmarks.name: Santi Luca e Martina
landmarks.info: Pietro da Cortona's church over the Forum, his own burial place.

landmarks.name: San Giovanni dei Fiorentini
landmarks.info: The Florentines' church at the bend of the Tiber, its dome by Carlo Maderno.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria in Vallicella
landmarks.info: St Philip Neri's Chiesa Nuova, 1575 to 1606, with Rubens's altarpieces.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria dei Miracoli
landmarks.info: One of the twin churches at the head of the Corso, facing Piazza del Popolo.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria in Montesanto
landmarks.info: The other twin, its dome twelve-sided because its site is narrower.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria del Popolo
landmarks.info: With Caravaggio's Conversion of St Paul and Crucifixion of St Peter in the Cerasi chapel.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria Maggiore
landmarks.info: One of the four papal basilicas, fifth century, its mosaics the oldest of the Virgin in Rome; one of its two chapel domes.

landmarks.name: Campanile of Santa Maria Maggiore
landmarks.info: The tallest bell tower in Rome, 75 m, 1377.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
landmarks.info: Perhaps the first church in Rome dedicated to the Virgin; the Romanesque tower and the mosaics on the front are twelfth century.

landmarks.name: Santa Maria in Cosmedin
landmarks.info: The Greek community's church, with the Bocca della Verità in its portico and a Romanesque tower of seven storeys.

landmarks.name: Santi Giovanni e Paolo
landmarks.info: On the Caelian, its twelfth-century tower standing on the foundations of the temple of Claudius.

landmarks.name: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza
landmarks.info: Borromini's chapel of the old university, 1642 to 1660: a star of David plan, and a spiral lantern climbing to a flame.

landmarks.name: The Great Synagogue
landmarks.info: Rome's synagogue, 1904, its square dome the only one of its kind in the city.

landmarks.name: San Giovanni in Laterano
landmarks.info: The cathedral of Rome - not St Peter's - and the mother of all churches; Galilei's front of 1735 carries fifteen statues seven metres high.

landmarks.name: Ponte Sant'Angelo (the arches)
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Sisto
landmarks.info: Sixtus IV's bridge of 1479, with its round eye in the middle pier to let the floods through.

landmarks.name: Ponte Fabricio
landmarks.info: 62 BC, and still carrying people over to the island: the oldest Roman bridge in the city in its first form.

landmarks.name: Ponte Cestio
landmarks.info: From the island to Trastevere; Roman, rebuilt in the 1890s with its middle arch from the old stones.

landmarks.name: Ponte Garibaldi
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Palatino
landmarks.info: 1890, beside the stump of Ponte Rotto.

landmarks.name: Ponte Umberto Primo
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Vittorio Emanuele Secondo
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Cavour
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Giuseppe Mazzini
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Principe Amedeo Savoia Aosta
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Regina Margherita
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Sublicio
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Testaccio
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Giacomo Matteotti
landmarks.info: A bridge over the Tiber, its arches and piers under the mapped deck.

landmarks.name: Ponte Rotto
landmarks.info: The Pons Aemilius of 179 BC, the first stone bridge over the Tiber; carried off by the floods time after time, it has stood as one broken arch in the river since 1598.

palette._: Rome's walls are stucco, not brick: ochre, yellow, terracotta, pink, cream; and travertine

_lakeColour: the Tiber is green; the fountain basins the map draws as water take it too

terrainCuts._: Via degli Annibaldi in its cutting through the Oppian spur, under the Ponte degli Annibaldi: the 12 m elevation grid smears the hill over it

roadWidths._: the avenue is mapped as a service road with no width

romeEvents._: src/rome/events.js: the Vespa rides from the Colosseum down Via dei Fori Imperiali, round Piazza Venezia and up the Corso

streetlife._: src/core/streetlife.js: shopfronts, cafés, façade dress, chimney smoke

courts._: src/core/courts.js: courtyard floors, wells, fountains, pots and porticoes; the named fountains; the ruins strewn

crowds._sites: [lat, lon, radius, how many, and for a model with no mapped footprint the radius to keep clear of]

vehicles._: src/core/traffic.js: per km of route, capped; only those within far metres are moved and drawn

paving._: sampietrini: basalt setts in fan arcs, laid by world position (see src/engine/stages/02-ground.js)

areaColours._: Rome's blocks are stone to the walls: no yards, so land use reads as paving, not grass

photo._: src/rome/photo.js: the photograph on the Ponte degli Annibaldi; #photo opens on it, in its 3:4 frame

dress._: src/core/dress.js: cornices, string courses, water towers, fire escapes, dormers, bay windows

_treeSpecies: Rome's trees: the stone pine and the cypress, the planes along the Tiber, holm oaks on the hills, oleander and bay in the gardens
_treeKeepOut: the Ponte degli Annibaldi: the photograph's view of the Colosseum stays open
